lines.trans: Lemon Tree Inn, good morning! Clara speaking.
Who is it? Another booking for the weekend?

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: One moment... hello, sir! Are you calling about the dark-blue suitcase?
Ask him what his name is! Write it down!
Yes, sir, we locked your suitcase in our closet. What is your name, please?
What is he saying? Why are you frowning?
Sir? He says: Please do not open the white parcel. I am coming Friday at noon.
Pass me the phone, let me speak with him!
Too late! He said thank you and hung up!
Polite voice? Young or older?
Soft, polite, around thirty-five. He sounded nervous, not angry.
Nervous about a wooden train? This story gets stranger every hour.

Ask him what his name is! Write it down!
Yes, sir, we locked your suitcase in our closet. What is your name, please?
What is he saying? Why are you frowning?
Sir? He says: Please do not open the white parcel. I am coming Friday at noon.

lines.trans: See you later!

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.
Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for writing down a note or phone number.

examples.text: Apunto la dirección en un papel.
examples.trans: I jot down the address on a piece of paper.
Did you write down the guest's name?

meanings.note: Tall storage closet or bedroom wardrobe.

examples.trans: The wardrobe is here.

examples.text: Vemos los armarios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wardrobes from the door.

meanings.note: Le atiende... is standard polite phone/desk phrasing in Spain.

examples.text: La encargada atiende el mostrador hoy.
examples.trans: La encargada is tending the front desk today.
They assisted us very kindly.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

meanings.note: Quedarse blanco means 'to go pale'.

examples.trans: It is a white piece.

examples.text: Mira, hay un sobre blanco doblado en el asa.
examples.trans: Look, there is a folded white envelope on the handle.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Invariable before masculine or feminine singular nouns (cada día, cada mañana).

examples.trans: I open the cafe every morning.
Each room has its own key.

meanings.note: Fruncir el ceño means 'to frown'.

examples.trans: The brow is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ceños desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the brows from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Faltan cinco minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve.

examples.text: Tenemos cinco mesas en el patio.
examples.trans: We have five tables in the courtyard.

colgar.gloss: to hang; to hang up (the phone)

meanings.en: to hang; to hang up (the phone)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuelgo) and g -> gu in preterite 1st sg (colgué).

examples.text: Cuelgo el abrigo detrás de la puerta.
examples.trans: I hang my coat behind the door.

examples.text: Colgó los farolillos entre las ramas.
examples.trans: He hung the lanterns among the branches.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.trans: What is your name?
How do I find the hardware shop?

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

demasiado.gloss: too much; too many; too (as adv)

meanings.en: too much; too many; too (as adv)
meanings.note: Agrees as a determiner before a noun (demasiado tiempo); invariable as an adverb before an adjective.

examples.trans: Three years was too much time.
Do not walk too fast.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: False friend: means 'polite', whereas 'educated' is culto or formado.

examples.trans: It is a polite piece.
Polite voice? Young or older?

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for feeling angry or upset with someone.

examples.trans: It is an angry piece.

examples.text: Suave, educada, de unos treinta y cinco años. Sonaba nervioso, no enfadado.
examples.trans: Soft, polite, around thirty-five. He sounded nervous, not angry.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Por fin = finally.

examples.trans: The end is here.

examples.text: Vemos los fines desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ends from the door.

fruncir.gloss: to wrinkle; to furrow (fruncir el ceño = to frown)

meanings.en: to wrinkle; to furrow (fruncir el ceño = to frown)
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> z before o (frunzo).

examples.text: Siempre frunces el ceño cuando lees.
examples.trans: You always wrinkle your brow when reading.

examples.text: Frunció el ceño al mirar la cuenta.
examples.trans: He frowned when looking at the bill.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Hablo con mi familia cada domingo.
examples.trans: I speak with my family every Sunday.

examples.text: Hablamos largo rato bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We talked for a long while under the tree.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Covers both a personal story and historical past.

examples.trans: The story is here.

examples.text: Vemos las historias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stories from the door.

meanings.note: Universal friendly greeting at any hour of the day.

examples.trans: Hello, come in and sit down!
Hi, how are you doing today?

meanings.note: ¿Qué hora es? asks the clock time.

examples.trans: The hour is here.

examples.text: Vemos las horas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hours from the door.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Plural lleva tilde: jóvenes; also used as a noun (el/la joven).

examples.trans: It is a young piece.
Polite voice? Young or older?

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Fruit tree bearing lemons (el limón -> el limonero).

examples.trans: The lemon tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limoneros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemon trees from the door.

llamar.gloss: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)

meanings.en: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)
meanings.note: ¿Cómo se llama? asks someone's name.

examples.trans: I am from here, pleased to meet you.
Someone called by phone yesterday.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.
See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; plural mayores.

examples.trans: It is an older piece.

examples.text: Conoces bien a los hermanos mayores, Mateo.
examples.trans: You know older brothers well, Mateo.

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.text: El mediodía es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The noon is very important here.
We talk about the noon.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Accented más means 'more / most'; de más = extra.

examples.trans: Would you like a little more tea?
It is the quietest room.

meanings.note: Ponerse nervioso = to get nervous.

examples.trans: It is a nervous piece.

examples.text: ¿Nervioso por un tren de madera? Esta historia es cada hora más rara.
examples.trans: Nervous about a wooden train? This story gets stranger every hour.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?
Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

meanings.note: Azul oscuro = dark blue; gris oscuro = dark grey.

examples.trans: It is a dark piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Wrapped package or parcel.

examples.trans: The parcel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los paquetes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the parcels from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Charming small inn with rooms around a courtyard.

examples.trans: The inn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las posadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inns from the door.

meanings.note: Preguntar asks a question; pedir asks for an item or favour.

examples.text: Pregunto en la farmacia por la calle.
examples.trans: I ask at the pharmacy about the street.

examples.text: Una clienta preguntó por el desayuno.
examples.trans: A guest asked about breakfast.

meanings.note: Plural quiénes; ¿de quién es? = whose is it?

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose blue suitcase is this?

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: ¡Qué raro! = How strange!

examples.trans: It is a strange piece.

examples.text: ¡Muy tranquilo! Aunque, ¿acaba de oír un golpe metálico raro?
examples.trans: Very peaceful! Though did you just hear a strange metallic knock?

meanings.note: Tener una reserva = to have a booking.

examples.trans: The reservation is here.

examples.text: Vemos las reservas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the reservations from the door.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Fin de semana = weekend; la semana que viene = next week.

examples.trans: The week is here.

examples.text: Vemos las semanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the weeks from the door.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a soft piece.

examples.text: Y mire: esta chaqueta de lana suave está limpia y nueva. Pruébela.
examples.trans: And look: this soft wool cardigan is clean and unworn. Try it on.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Por teléfono = by phone / on the phone.

examples.trans: The telephone is here.

examples.text: Vemos los teléfonos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the telephones from the door.

meanings.note: Treinta y cinco = thirty-five.

examples.text: Nos dan treinta días de plazo.
examples.trans: They give us thirty days' notice.

examples.text: Son las nueve y treinta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is nine thirty-five.

meanings.note: Plural los trenes.

examples.trans: The train is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trains from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

meanings.note: Plural las voces; en voz baja = in a low voice.

examples.trans: The voice is here.

examples.text: Vemos las voces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the voices from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Accented él ('he/him') is distinct from unaccented article el ('the').

examples.trans: He works at City Hall.

examples.text: Sube a hablar con él un minuto.
examples.trans: Go upstairs and talk to him for a minute.
